intro: There is a reason the Machame Route accounts for more Kilimanjaro summits than any other trail on the mountain.

It is not the easiest route. It is not the shortest. But it is, without question, the most rewarding — a seven-day wilderness expedition through five of Kilimanjaro's most dramatic ecological zones, built around a proven acclimatisation strategy that has delivered summit successes for generations of climbers.

The Machame earns its nickname — the Whiskey Route — not because it is intoxicating (though it is), but because it demands something of you. By the time you stand at Uhuru Peak at 5,895 metres, you will have earned every metre of that altitude.

whyChoose.title: The acclimatisation profile works.
whyChoose.body: The Machame's 'climb high, sleep low' strategy — ascending to 4,630m at Lava Tower on Day 3, then descending to Barranco Camp at 3,900m — is one of the most effective altitude management techniques available on a 7-day route.

whyChoose.title: The scenery is extraordinary.
whyChoose.body: No other route on Kilimanjaro transitions through such dramatically different landscapes in a single day — equatorial rainforest, open heather moorland, the vast Shira Plateau, Alpine desert, and glacial terrain.

whyChoose.title: The Barranco Wall is unlike anything else.
whyChoose.body: A 300-metre near-vertical scramble at dawn that looks terrifying and proves magnificent — hands and feet, exposed sections, and a grin you cannot remove for the rest of the day.

whyChoose.title: The route prepares you properly for summit night.
whyChoose.body: By the time you reach Barafu Base Camp on Day 5, your body has spent four days at progressively higher altitude. Summit night, while never easy, feels manageable rather than brutal.

machame.arrivalDay: You arrive in Tanzania and transfer to your hotel in Arusha or Moshi. Your lead guide meets you for a thorough pre-climb briefing — gear check, route overview, altitude safety protocol, and Q&A. Rest well. Hydrate. Sleep early. Your expedition begins tomorrow.

itinerary.title: Machame Gate → Machame Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Machame Camp · Elevation: 3,026m · Distance: 11 km · Hiking Time: 5–7 hours
itinerary.body: The longest Day 1 of any standard Kilimanjaro route. From Machame Gate at 1,800m, the trail enters the rainforest immediately and does not hold back. Colobus monkeys move through the trees overhead. Camp sits on a moorland ridge above the treeline, where the stars, on a clear night, are extraordinary.
itinerary.expect: Your first full day of trail. Legs will feel it. Eat well, drink more water than you think you need, and sleep as early as possible.

itinerary.title: Machame Camp → Shira Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Shira Camp · Elevation: 3,766m · Distance: 5 km · Hiking Time: 4–6 hours
itinerary.body: The forest thins and the world opens. Vegetation transforms to open heather and moorland, and the Shira Plateau opens ahead: vast, windswept, ancient. Kibo's glaciated summit rises on the horizon.
itinerary.expect: A shorter day after Day 1's effort. Afternoon fatigue is normal. Mild headaches are common at this altitude — they usually resolve overnight.

itinerary.title: Shira Camp → Lava Tower → Barranco Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Barranco Camp · Elevation: 3,983m · Distance: 10 km · Hiking Time: 6–8 hours
itinerary.body: The most important day on the Machame Route. The morning climbs to the Lava Tower at 4,630m — the 'climb high, sleep low' strategy in action. Then the trail drops nearly 700 metres to Barranco Camp, with dramatic views of the Barranco Wall looming above.
itinerary.expect: This is the day altitude makes itself felt. Appetite may decrease. Headaches are common. Tell your guide immediately if symptoms feel significant.

itinerary.title: Barranco Camp → Barranco Wall → Karanga Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Karanga Camp · Elevation: 3,995m · Distance: 5 km · Hiking Time: 4–5 hours
itinerary.body: The Barranco Wall awaits — a 300-metre rocky scramble that has become one of Kilimanjaro's most iconic sections. The afternoon crosses the Karanga Valley, the last reliable water source on the mountain.
itinerary.expect: An exhilarating morning followed by a satisfying afternoon. Energy typically returns after the altitude adjustment of Day 3.

itinerary.title: Karanga Camp → Barafu Base Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Barafu Camp · Elevation: 4,673m · Distance: 4 km · Hiking Time: 3–4 hours
itinerary.body: The shortest hiking day of the expedition. The trail climbs through Alpine desert to Barafu — Kilimanjaro's main high camp at 4,673m. Your guide conducts the full summit briefing. At midnight, the alarm sounds.
itinerary.expect: Anticipation, nerves, and altitude-related restlessness are completely normal. Rest even if you cannot sleep. Eat the full dinner even if appetite is low.

itinerary.title: Summit Night → Uhuru Peak → Mweka Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Mweka Camp · Elevation: 3,110m · Ascent: 5 km · Descent: 12 km · Total Time: 10–14 hours
itinerary.body: Midnight. Your guide sets the pace — pole pole. At Stella Point (5,739m), the first light of dawn breaks across the Indian Ocean. Forty-five minutes later — Uhuru Peak. Africa, 5,895 metres below your feet. The descent continues all the way to Mweka Camp.
itinerary.expect: Summit night is the hardest physical and mental challenge of the expedition. It is also, without exception, the most rewarding.

itinerary.title: Mweka Camp → Mweka Gate → Hotel
itinerary.meta: End of Expedition · Elevation: 1,640m · Distance: 10 km · Hiking Time: 3–4 hours
itinerary.body: The final morning through the rainforest. At Mweka Gate, your summit certificate is presented by your guide. Your driver meets you for the transfer back to your hotel.
itinerary.expect: Rest. Celebrate. The mountain is behind you. The memory is permanent.

machame.arrivalDay6Day: Arrive at Kilimanjaro International Airport, where your guide meets you for the transfer to your lodge in Moshi. Settle in, then meet your guides in the evening for a full trek briefing and equipment check ahead of tomorrow's start. Rest well — your expedition begins in the morning.

itinerary6Day.title: Machame Gate → Machame Camp
itinerary6Day.meta: Camp: Machame Camp · Elevation: 3,050m · Distance: 11 km · Hiking Time: 5–7 hours
itinerary6Day.body: A roughly 60-minute drive from Moshi to Machame Gate at 1,830m, passing through Machame township on the mountain's lower slopes. From the gate, the trail climbs steadily through rainforest to Machame Camp on a moorland ridge above the treeline — gaiters and trekking poles are worth having, since the lower trail can be muddy.
itinerary6Day.expect: The longest Day 1 of any standard Kilimanjaro route. Legs will feel it. Eat well, drink more water than you think you need, and sleep as early as possible.

itinerary6Day.title: Machame Camp → Shira Camp
itinerary6Day.meta: Camp: Shira Camp · Elevation: 3,850m · Distance: 5 km · Hiking Time: 4–6 hours
itinerary6Day.body: Leaving the rainforest glades behind, the trail climbs a steep rocky ridge across the valley before turning west into open heather moorland to reach Shira Camp on the vast Shira Plateau.
itinerary6Day.expect: A shorter day after Day 1's effort. Afternoon fatigue is normal. Mild headaches are common at this altitude — they usually resolve overnight.

itinerary6Day.title: Shira Camp → Lava Tower → Barranco Camp
itinerary6Day.meta: Camp: Barranco Camp · Elevation: 4,000m · Distance: 10 km · Hiking Time: 5–6 hours
itinerary6Day.body: East along the Shira Plateau past the junction toward Kibo's peak, then southeast to Lava Tower — the 'Shark's Tooth' at 4,650m — before descending to Barranco Camp. You'll finish near the elevation you started at, but this day is essential acclimatisation for what's ahead.
itinerary6Day.expect: This is the day altitude makes itself felt. Appetite may decrease. Headaches are common. Tell your guide immediately if symptoms feel significant.

itinerary6Day.title: Barranco Camp → Barranco Wall → Barafu Camp
itinerary6Day.meta: Camp: Barafu Camp · Elevation: 4,700m · Distance: 9 km · Hiking Time: 6–8 hours
itinerary6Day.body: The Barranco Wall leads up through the Karanga Valley — the last reliable water source on the mountain — and on to the junction with the Mweka Trail, completing the South Circuit with views of the summit from multiple angles, before reaching Barafu Camp. This is the longest day on the 6-day route, combining what the 7-day itinerary splits across two days.
itinerary6Day.expect: The most demanding day on this itinerary. Take it steadily — your acclimatisation from previous days carries you through. Your guide conducts the full summit briefing on arrival.

itinerary6Day.title: Summit Night → Uhuru Peak → Mweka Camp
itinerary6Day.meta: Camp: Mweka Camp · Elevation: 5,895m summit → 3,090m · Distance: 5 km up / 13 km down · Hiking Time: 10–14 hours total
itinerary6Day.body: Departing between midnight and 2 AM, you'll climb between the Rebmann and Ratzel glaciers toward Stella Point on the crater rim — the most physically and mentally demanding stretch of the climb, rewarded with one of the finest sunrises on the mountain. From Stella Point, a further hour — often through snow — brings you to Uhuru Peak, the highest point in Africa. Descend past Barafu for a lunch stop, continuing to Mweka Camp for your final night on the mountain.
itinerary6Day.expect: Summit night is the hardest physical and mental challenge of the expedition. It is also, without exception, the most rewarding.

itinerary6Day.title: Mweka Camp → Mweka Gate → Hotel
itinerary6Day.meta: End of Expedition · Elevation: 1,680m · Distance: 10 km · Hiking Time: 3–4 hours
itinerary6Day.body: Descend to Mweka Gate to collect your summit certificate. Lower elevations can be wet and muddy — gaiters and poles help. Our team meets you at the gate for the drive back to your hotel in Moshi (~60 minutes).
itinerary6Day.expect: Rest. Celebrate. The mountain is behind you. The memory is permanent.

choosing.intro: Both itineraries follow the same trail up Kilimanjaro's southern slope and share Machame's core appeal — five distinct ecological zones and a proven 'climb high, sleep low' acclimatisation strategy. The difference comes down to pace, and how much time your body gets to adjust to altitude before summit night.

items.label: 6-Day Machame
items.desc: Our fastest Machame option, combining the Barranco–Karanga–Barafu stretch into a single, longer climbing day. Best suited to climbers who've been at high altitude recently, or those with strong trekking fitness and a tighter schedule. The compressed acclimatisation window means a somewhat lower success rate — worth weighing against the extra day saved.

items.label: 7-Day Machame
items.desc: Our recommended default. Splits the Barranco Wall, Karanga Valley, and approach to Barafu across two full days rather than one, giving your body meaningfully more time to adjust before summit night. The right call for most climbers, including many first-timers.

choosing.footer: Whichever you choose, physical preparation beforehand matters more than the day count — arriving fit makes every version of this climb safer and more enjoyable.

highlights.title: The Barranco Wall
highlights.body: A dramatic 300-metre rock scramble that looks far more intimidating than it actually is — no technical climbing skill required, just some hands-on scrambling and a head for the exposure. The view from the top, looking back across the valley, is one of the best on the mountain.

highlights.title: Lava Tower ("Shark's Tooth")
highlights.body: A striking volcanic plug rising to 4,650m, visited as part of the acclimatisation detour before descending to Barranco. It's one of Kilimanjaro's most photographed landmarks, and the centrepiece of the 'climb high, sleep low' profile that makes Machame's acclimatisation so effective.

faq.q: Is the 6-day Machame route right for a first Kilimanjaro attempt?
faq.a: It's best suited to climbers with some recent high-altitude experience or strong trekking fitness, since it compresses two acclimatisation days into one. First-time high-altitude climbers are generally better served by our 7-day version, which splits the Barranco Wall, Karanga Valley, and approach to Barafu across two full days.

faq.q: Why is Machame called the "Whiskey Route"?
faq.a: It's a nickname reflecting its reputation as a tougher, more rewarding climb compared to the gentler Marangu Route (nicknamed the "Coca-Cola Route"). Unlike Marangu's hut accommodation, Machame climbers camp in tents the entire way.

faq.q: What's the summit success rate on the 6-day Machame route?
faq.a: Generally in the 80–85% range — solid, though somewhat lower than the 7-day version's ~85–90%, given the reduced acclimatisation time. The tradeoff is a shorter, more efficient trip for climbers who can handle the pace.

faq.q: Do I need technical climbing experience?
faq.a: No — Machame is a walking route throughout, including the Barranco Wall scramble. General fitness and some outdoor experience make the days more enjoyable, particularly summit night.

faq.q: What's the best time of year to climb Machame?
faq.a: The dry seasons — late June through October, and December through February — offer the most stable weather and clearest views.

faq.q: Can I extend this trip with a safari or Zanzibar stay?
faq.a: Yes — many climbers add a safari or beach extension either before or after the climb, making efficient use of the trip to Tanzania.

intro: If you ask an experienced Kilimanjaro guide which route they would choose for themselves, the answer, more often than not, is the Lemosho.

The Lemosho is Kilimanjaro's most complete wilderness experience — beginning in one of the most pristine and rarely-walked sections of forest on the entire mountain and traversing the full southern circuit before the midnight push to Uhuru Peak. A deliberate, measured acclimatisation strategy translates directly into Kilimanjaro's highest summit success rate of any standard route.
One extra day on the mountain. One dedicated acclimatisation rest. A success rate of 90–95%. For most climbers, that is the best investment they will make on the entire expedition.

whyChoose.title: The acclimatisation is exceptional.
whyChoose.body: Day 3 is a rest and short-hike day on the Shira Plateau at 3,810m — an extra 24+ hours at altitude before ascending further. That difference shows most clearly on summit morning.

whyChoose.title: The trail is quieter.
whyChoose.body: The approach through the Londorossi forest reserve is one of Kilimanjaro's least-trafficked sections. From Day 1 to Day 3, you are unlikely to encounter another climbing party.

whyChoose.title: The entry through Londorossi is extraordinary.
whyChoose.body: Buffalo are regularly encountered on the lower approach. The forest is ancient, dense, and truly wild.

whyChoose.title: It joins the Machame circuit on Day 4.
whyChoose.body: After the quiet wilderness approach, you merge with the iconic southern circuit and experience the Barranco Wall, Karanga Valley, and the full summit route.

lemosho.arrivalDay: Transfer from Kilimanjaro International Airport to your hotel. Your lead guide meets you for a thorough pre-climb briefing — gear check, route overview, altitude safety protocol, and summit strategy. Come with questions.

itinerary.title: Londorossi Gate → Big Tree Camp (Mti Mkubwa)
itinerary.meta: Camp: Mti Mkubwa · Elevation: 2,650m · Distance: 6 km · Hiking Time: 2–3 hours
itinerary.body: A gentle, deliberate opening day. From Londorossi Gate at 2,100m, the trail enters the Lemosho's most distinctive feature — a section of forest so pristine it feels genuinely untouched. Buffalo tracks cross the path.
itinerary.expect: The shortest hiking day of the route. Use the afternoon to rest, explore the forest edge, and adjust to the change in altitude.

itinerary.title: Mti Mkubwa → Shira Ridge → Shira 1 Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Shira 1 Camp · Elevation: 3,500m · Distance: 8 km · Hiking Time: 4–6 hours
itinerary.body: The forest retreats and the mountain reveals itself. The trail climbs onto the open heather and moorland of the Shira Ridge. At the top, the Shira Plateau opens ahead — vast, ancient, otherworldly.
itinerary.expect: A sustained climb with significant altitude gain. Headaches are common tonight — the body's normal response to ascending 1,400m in a single day.

itinerary.title: Shira 1 → Shira 2 Camp (Acclimatisation Day)
itinerary.meta: Camp: Shira 2 Camp · Elevation: 3,810m · Distance: 8 km · Hiking Time: 4–5 hours
itinerary.body: This is the day that separates the Lemosho from every other route on the mountain. A shorter morning hike delivers you to camp by early afternoon — the rest of the day is yours, and it is the most productive acclimatisation available on any standard route.
itinerary.expect: The most important rest day of the expedition. Embrace it. Eat well. Drink 4 litres of water.

itinerary.title: Shira 2 → Lava Tower → Barranco Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Barranco Camp · Elevation: 3,983m · Distance: 10 km · Hiking Time: 6–8 hours
itinerary.body: The Lemosho joins the Machame circuit today. The route climbs to the Lava Tower at 4,630m, then descends 700 metres to Barranco Camp. Your Lemosho-acclimatised body handles this altitude with noticeably more ease.
itinerary.expect: A long and demanding day, but one where your acclimatisation advantage begins to show. Energy and appetite typically remain strong.

itinerary.title: Barranco Wall → Karanga Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Karanga Camp · Elevation: 3,995m · Distance: 5 km · Hiking Time: 4–5 hours
itinerary.body: The Barranco Wall — 300 metres of near-vertical scramble requiring hands and feet throughout. The afternoon crosses the Karanga Valley, the last water source on the mountain.
itinerary.expect: An exhilarating morning that typically restores energy after the altitude adjustment days.

itinerary.title: Karanga Camp → Barafu Base Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Barafu Camp · Elevation: 4,673m · Distance: 4 km · Hiking Time: 3–4 hours
itinerary.body: The final approach to base camp, perched on a rocky spine at 4,673m. Your guide conducts the full summit night briefing. At midnight, the alarm sounds.
itinerary.expect: A short hike followed by a long wait. Trust your preparation — six days of steady acclimatisation have done their work.

itinerary.title: Summit Night → Uhuru Peak → Mweka Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Mweka Camp · Elevation: 3,110m · Ascent: 5 km · Descent: 12 km · Total Time: 10–14 hours
itinerary.body: Midnight departure toward the crater rim. Stella Point arrives at 5,739m as the sun breaks across the Indian Ocean. Forty-five minutes later — Uhuru Peak. You are on the Roof of Africa.
itinerary.expect: The hardest and most extraordinary day of the expedition. Everything that came before was preparation for this.

itinerary.title: Mweka Camp → Mweka Gate → Hotel
itinerary.meta: End of Expedition · Elevation: 1,640m · Distance: 10 km · Hiking Time: 3–4 hours
itinerary.body: One final morning in the forest. At Mweka Gate, your summit certificate is presented. Your driver waits.
itinerary.expect: Rest. Celebrate. You have climbed Kilimanjaro.

items.label: 8-Day Lemosho
items.desc: The highest-success option. Adds a full extra acclimatisation day and begins on foot in the tropical forest rather than by vehicle. Gives your body the most time to adjust to altitude, meaningfully lowering the risk of altitude sickness — the right call if you haven't trekked in a while, or simply want the best possible odds of reaching Uhuru Peak.

choosing.footer: Whichever you choose, physical preparation beforehand matters more than the day count — arriving fit makes every version of this climb safer and more enjoyable.

highlights.title: Cathedral Peak
highlights.body: A dramatic rock formation rising to 3,872m (12,703ft) on the Shira Plateau, reachable via an optional acclimatisation side-hike. It's one of the best viewpoints on the entire route — and because it's a there-and-back detour, it doubles as smart altitude prep without adding net elevation gain for the day.

highlights.title: Dendrosenecio kilimanjari
highlights.body: Keep an eye out on the moorland stretches for this giant groundsel — a strange, tree-like plant found almost nowhere else on Earth outside East Africa's high-altitude zones. It's one of Kilimanjaro's more surreal sights, and a favourite photo stop for climbers crossing the Shira Plateau.

faq.q: How do I choose between the 6-, 7-, and 8-day Lemosho itineraries?
faq.a: It comes down to altitude experience and how much time you have. The 6-day route is best suited to climbers who've been at high altitude recently or have strong trekking fitness — not recommended as a first Kilimanjaro attempt, since it compresses two acclimatisation days into one. The 7-day is our most popular choice and recommended default — solid for anyone with general trekking experience. The 8-day adds a further acclimatisation day, giving you the highest achievable success rate.

Not technically — the terrain is similar where the routes overlap. Lemosho's advantage is a longer, gentler acclimatisation profile and lower crowds in the early days, which generally makes it feel more manageable, not harder.

faq.q: What's the summit success rate on Lemosho?
faq.a: It varies by duration: the 6-day sees around 75–80%, the 7-day 85–90%, and the 8-day consistently 90–95% — among the highest of any standard route on the mountain.

faq.q: Do I need prior hiking experience for Lemosho?
faq.a: No technical climbing skill is required on any Lemosho itinerary — it's a walking route throughout. That said, general fitness and some outdoor experience make the days more enjoyable, especially on summit night.

faq.q: What's the best time of year to climb via Lemosho?
faq.a: The dry seasons — late June through October, and December through February — offer the most stable weather and clearest views. The route is walkable outside those windows, though with a higher chance of rain and cloud cover on the lower slopes.

faq.q: Can I combine a Lemosho climb with a safari or Zanzibar extension?
faq.a: Yes — many climbers add a safari or beach stay either before or after their trek. Since you'll already be acclimatised to Tanzania's time zone and travel rhythm, it's an efficient way to extend the trip.

intro: Most people who climb Kilimanjaro climb from the south. The Rongai goes the other way.

Approaching from the north — from the Kenyan border — the Rongai offers a Kilimanjaro experience that is fundamentally different from any other route on the mountain. The ecosystem is drier and more open. The trail is quieter by a significant margin. Wildlife on the lower slopes — elephant, buffalo, eland — makes the first days feel closer to a wilderness game walk than a mountain approach.
For climbers tackling Kilimanjaro during Tanzania's wet season months (March–May), when the south face is drenched and slippery, the Rongai's northern approach stays dry and firm throughout.

whyChoose.title: The solitude is real.
whyChoose.body: On some days of the Rongai, you will encounter no other climbing party. For solo climbers and small groups who value genuine wilderness, this matters.

whyChoose.title: The wildlife is exceptional.
whyChoose.body: Elephant, buffalo, zebra, and eland are regularly encountered on the lower northern slopes — a wildlife experience no southern route provides.

whyChoose.title: It is the only viable route during the long rains.
whyChoose.body: April and May are wet season months on the southern slopes — muddy and demanding. The Rongai's northern exposure stays dry. Not a compromise — the correct choice.

whyChoose.title: The gradient is steadier.
whyChoose.body: The Rongai ascends with a more gradual, linear profile than the Machame or Lemosho. No scrambling sections, no exposed ridgeline traverses.

rongai.arrivalDay: You arrive in Tanzania and transfer to your hotel. Your guide conducts a full pre-climb briefing — gear check, route overview, altitude safety protocols, and Q&A. The Rongai begins further from Arusha than other routes, so we brief you thoroughly on the drive to the gate the following morning.

itinerary.title: Rongai Gate → Simba Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Simba Camp · Elevation: 2,625m · Distance: 7 km · Hiking Time: 3–4 hours
itinerary.body: The drive from Moshi to Rongai Gate takes you through the Kenyan border zone — open savannah, Maasai settlements, and the first distant views of Kilimanjaro's northern slopes. From the gate, the trail enters dry, open forest.
itinerary.expect: A gentle, wildlife-rich opening day. The Rongai's lower elevation gain on Day 1 makes for a more comfortable start.

itinerary.title: Simba Camp → Second Cave Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Second Cave Camp · Elevation: 3,450m · Distance: 9 km · Hiking Time: 4–6 hours
itinerary.body: The trail climbs through steadily changing vegetation — open woodland gives way to moorland and the first giant lobelias appear. Views extend north across the Kenyan plains and south toward Mawenzi.
itinerary.expect: A longer day with steady altitude gain. The altitude begins to register tonight — drink 4 litres of water and eat a full dinner.

itinerary.title: Second Cave Camp → Kikelewa Cave Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Kikelewa Cave Camp · Elevation: 3,600m · Distance: 5 km · Hiking Time: 3–4 hours
itinerary.body: A shorter day designed for acclimatisation. The trail continues through open moorland, stark and beautiful, with Mawenzi Peak dominating the eastern horizon. Your guide recommends an afternoon acclimatisation walk.
itinerary.expect: A restful day with significant altitude exposure. Use the afternoon to explore and acclimatise rather than rest passively.

itinerary.title: Kikelewa Cave → Mawenzi Tarn Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Mawenzi Tarn Camp · Elevation: 4,330m · Distance: 4 km · Hiking Time: 3–5 hours
itinerary.body: The trail climbs steeply to Mawenzi Tarn — a glacial lake beneath the dramatic spires of Mawenzi Peak. This is the Rongai's equivalent of the Lava Tower stop — a significant altitude reach before descending to sleep.
itinerary.expect: The altitude makes itself felt clearly at 4,330m. Headaches are common and normal.

itinerary.title: Mawenzi Tarn → Kibo Hut (Base Camp)
itinerary.meta: Camp: Kibo Hut · Elevation: 4,703m · Distance: 9 km · Hiking Time: 4–6 hours
itinerary.body: The long saddle crossing between Mawenzi and Kibo — a lunar landscape of volcanic dust and pumice. Kibo Hut at 4,703m is a stone building rather than a tent, unique to the Rongai on this section.
itinerary.expect: The saddle crossing is mentally demanding — long, exposed, and at significant altitude. Take it slowly.

itinerary.title: Summit Night → Uhuru Peak → Horombo Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Horombo Camp · Elevation: 3,720m · Ascent: 5 km · Descent: 12 km · Total Time: 10–14 hours
itinerary.body: The Rongai's summit route approaches from the north and east, reaching the crater rim at Gilman's Point (5,681m) before the crater rim walk to Uhuru Peak. The descent returns via the southern route to Horombo Camp.
itinerary.expect: The Rongai's summit night is considered slightly more technically demanding due to the steeper northern slope.

itinerary.title: Horombo Camp → Marangu Gate → Hotel
itinerary.meta: End of Expedition · Elevation: 1,860m · Distance: 19 km · Hiking Time: 5–7 hours
itinerary.body: A long final day through moorland and rainforest to the gate, ending at Marangu Gate where your certificate awaits. Transfer back to your hotel.
itinerary.expect: The Rongai is behind you. The story is not.

intro: Every mountain has a classic. For Kilimanjaro, it is the Marangu.

The oldest established route on the mountain, the Marangu has been carrying climbers toward Uhuru Peak since the earliest days of organised Kilimanjaro expeditions. The three permanent huts — Mandara, Horombo, and Kibo — have stood for decades. The Marangu is also the only route where climbers sleep in permanent mountain huts rather than tents.

We want to be honest with you: the Marangu's summit success rate of approximately 65–70% is the lowest of our four routes — a structural characteristic of the route's faster ascent profile. For experienced trekkers who understand this trade-off, the Marangu is a worthy and historic choice. For first-time high-altitude climbers prioritising summit success, we recommend the Lemosho or Machame. Choose the Marangu because you want the classic. Choose it with open eyes.

whyChoose.title: The hut accommodation is unique.
whyChoose.body: Mandara Hut at 2,720m, Horombo Hut at 3,720m, and Kibo Hut at 4,703m are the only permanent structures available on any Kilimanjaro route.

whyChoose.title: It is Kilimanjaro's most historically significant route.
whyChoose.body: The Marangu was the first route opened for organised climbing expeditions. The earliest recorded summits of the mountain were made via this path.

whyChoose.title: The same-path ascent and descent.
whyChoose.body: Unlike other routes, the Marangu ascends and descends via the same trail — a logistical simplicity that some climbers appreciate.

whyChoose.title: The most accessible price.
whyChoose.body: Hut accommodation, shared between multiple groups, reduces the equipment requirement — making it the most affordable option without sacrificing guide quality or safety.

marangu.arrivalDay: Transfer from Kilimanjaro Airport to your hotel. Full pre-climb briefing with your lead guide — gear check, route overview, hut accommodation details, altitude safety protocol, and Q&A. The Marangu Gate is the closest of any route to Moshi.

itinerary.title: Marangu Gate → Mandara Hut
itinerary.meta: Camp: Mandara Hut · Elevation: 2,720m · Distance: 8 km · Hiking Time: 3–4 hours
itinerary.body: From Marangu Gate at 1,860m, the trail enters the rainforest and climbs steadily through one of Kilimanjaro's most beautiful forest sections. Mandara Hut is a cluster of A-frame huts in a forest clearing. A short afternoon walk to Maundi Crater is recommended.
itinerary.expect: A comfortable first day with moderate altitude gain. The huts are often shared with other climbing groups — embrace the camaraderie.

itinerary.title: Mandara Hut → Horombo Hut
itinerary.meta: Camp: Horombo Hut · Elevation: 3,720m · Distance: 12 km · Hiking Time: 5–7 hours
itinerary.body: The forest gives way to moorland as the trail climbs steadily to Horombo — a long day with significant altitude gain, the Marangu's most testing section. Mawenzi Peak appears to the east.
itinerary.expect: The longest and most demanding day. Altitude headaches are common at Horombo. Eat a full dinner, drink 4 litres of water, and sleep as early as possible.

itinerary.title: Horombo Hut → Kibo Hut (Base Camp)
itinerary.meta: Camp: Kibo Hut · Elevation: 4,703m · Distance: 10 km · Hiking Time: 5–6 hours
itinerary.body: The moorland gives way to the saddle — a vast, flat, volcanic landscape between Mawenzi and Kibo. Kibo Hut at 4,703m is a stone building, austere and windswept, perched directly below the summit cone.
itinerary.expect: A demanding day with significant altitude impact. Listen carefully to your body and report any concerning symptoms to your guide.

itinerary.title: Summit Night → Uhuru Peak → Horombo Hut
itinerary.meta: Return to Horombo Hut · Elevation: 3,720m · Ascent: 5 km · Descent: 15 km · Total Time: 10–14 hours
itinerary.body: Midnight departure from Kibo Hut. The summit trail climbs steeply through volcanic scree toward Gilman's Point (5,681m). The crater rim walk west to Uhuru Peak delivers the mountain's ultimate reward. The descent returns the same way to Horombo Hut.
itinerary.expect: The hardest day of the expedition. The Marangu's faster ascent profile means summit night requires particular mental resilience and physical determination.

itinerary.title: Horombo Hut → Marangu Gate → Hotel
itinerary.meta: End of Expedition · Elevation: 1,860m · Distance: 20 km · Hiking Time: 5–7 hours
itinerary.body: The final descent through moorland and rainforest — a long, satisfying walk back to the gate where the expedition began. At Marangu Gate, your summit certificate is presented.
itinerary.expect: You finish where you started, the mountain completing a full circle.

intro: Most climbers approach Kilimanjaro looking for the best chance at the summit. Umbwe climbers are looking for something else entirely — the mountain's rawest, most direct test.

This is the steepest and most demanding standard route on Kilimanjaro, climbing straight up through dense rainforest before joining the southern circuit at Barranco Camp. There is no easing into this one.
We only recommend the Umbwe to experienced trekkers who already understand what altitude does to the body and want the quietest, most physically honest route to Uhuru Peak — not the easiest one.

quickFacts.trailTraffic: Low (increases after merging with the Machame Route at Barranco)

whyChoose.title: It is the most direct line to the mountain.
whyChoose.body: No long approach, no gentle warm-up — Umbwe climbs straight into the rainforest and keeps climbing. If you want the shortest distance between the gate and the glaciers, this is it.

whyChoose.title: The solitude is genuine, at least at first.
whyChoose.body: Umbwe sees far fewer climbers than Machame or Lemosho on its lower slopes. You'll have the forest largely to yourself until the route merges with the southern circuit at Barranco Camp.

whyChoose.title: The 7-day version adds the acclimatisation day Umbwe is missing.
whyChoose.body: The steep, fast ascent that makes Umbwe famous is also its biggest risk — this itinerary inserts a dedicated rest day at Barranco Camp before the Wall, giving your body real time to adjust before the summit push.

whyChoose.title: It rewards climbers who already know what they're doing.
whyChoose.body: This is not a first Kilimanjaro climb. We recommend the Umbwe to trekkers with prior high-altitude experience who want the mountain's most demanding standard route, eyes open.

umbwe.arrivalDay: You arrive in Tanzania and transfer to your hotel in Moshi. Your lead guide meets you for a thorough pre-climb briefing — gear check, route overview, altitude safety protocol, and Q&A. The Umbwe's steep opening days deserve extra attention here. Rest well and sleep early — your expedition begins tomorrow.

itinerary.title: Umbwe Gate → Umbwe Cave Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Umbwe Cave Camp · Elevation: 2,850m · Distance: 11 km · Hiking Time: 5–6 hours
itinerary.body: The steepest opening day of any standard Kilimanjaro route. From Umbwe Gate, the trail climbs immediately and relentlessly through dense rainforest — a steep forestry track with little flat ground. Watch the canopy for colobus monkeys as you climb.
itinerary.expect: This is a demanding first day with no easing in. Pace yourself, drink plenty of water, and expect to feel the climb in your legs by camp.

itinerary.title: Umbwe Cave Camp → Barranco Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Barranco Camp · Elevation: 3,900m · Distance: 6 km · Hiking Time: 4–5 hours
itinerary.body: The forest recedes into moorland as the trail follows the Umbwe Ridge in a steady ascent. By afternoon you reach Barranco Camp, where the Umbwe joins the Machame route's southern circuit — the solitude of the first two days gives way to a busier, more sociable camp.
itinerary.expect: Altitude gain is significant over two fast days — mild headaches are common. Report anything more serious to your guide.

itinerary.title: Acclimatisation Day at Barranco Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Barranco Camp · Elevation: 3,900m · Distance: Short acclimatisation walk · Hiking Time: Flexible
itinerary.body: A dedicated rest day — the one addition the 7-day Umbwe makes over the faster 6-day version, and the reason we recommend it. Use the day to explore the valley at a gentle pace, rest, and let your body catch up with the altitude before the Wall.
itinerary.expect: This is the most important day of the climb for your summit chances. Rest actively rather than passively — a short walk helps more than lying still.

itinerary.title: Barranco Wall → Karanga Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Karanga Camp · Elevation: 3,995m · Distance: 5 km · Hiking Time: 3–4 hours
itinerary.body: The Barranco Wall — a steep scramble up a 250-metre cliff face — greets you first thing in the morning. It looks harder than it is with hands and feet. Beyond the Wall, the trail continues into the Karanga Valley for a final steep stretch to camp.
itinerary.expect: A short but intense morning followed by an easier afternoon. Energy is often better today after the rest day.

itinerary.title: Karanga Camp → Barafu Base Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Barafu Camp · Elevation: 4,673m · Distance: 4 km · Hiking Time: 3–4 hours
itinerary.body: The trail completes the Southern Circuit, offering views of the summit from nearly every angle, before climbing through alpine desert to Barafu — Kilimanjaro's main high camp. Your guide conducts the full summit briefing before an early dinner and attempted sleep.
itinerary.expect: A short hiking day but a mentally significant one. Rest even if you can't sleep — midnight comes fast.

itinerary.title: Summit Night → Uhuru Peak → Mweka Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Mweka Camp · Elevation: 3,110m · Ascent: 5 km · Descent: 13 km · Total Time: 10–13 hours
itinerary.body: Midnight. The route climbs a steep, loose trail past the Rebmann and Ratzel Glaciers toward Stella Point, rewarded with sunrise over the crater rim. From there it's a further push through snow to Uhuru Peak. The descent is long, continuing all the way down to Mweka Camp.
itinerary.expect: The hardest day of the expedition, and the most rewarding. The descent afterward is long — pace yourself on tired legs.

itinerary.title: Mweka Camp → Mweka Gate → Hotel
itinerary.meta: End of Expedition · Elevation: 1,640m · Distance: 10 km · Hiking Time: 3–4 hours
itinerary.body: The final descent continues through rainforest to Mweka Gate, where your certificate is presented. Your driver returns you to your hotel in Moshi.
itinerary.expect: Rest. Celebrate. The mountain is behind you.

intro: Most Kilimanjaro routes take the most direct line to the summit. The Northern Circuit takes the long way round — deliberately.

This is the longest standard route on the mountain, circling from the western Lemosho approach around Kibo's rarely-visited northern slopes before turning south to the summit. The extra days buy something few other routes can offer: time. Time to acclimatise properly, time to see terrain almost no other climbers see, and time to simply be on the mountain rather than racing across it.

Right now, the Northern Circuit remains one of Kilimanjaro's quietest routes — a genuine wilderness circumnavigation for climbers who want the best possible preparation for summit night and the most complete view of the mountain along the way.

whyChoose.title: It is Kilimanjaro's longest — and most complete — route.
whyChoose.body: Nine days on the mountain means more time at altitude than any other standard route, translating directly into one of the highest summit success rates available.

whyChoose.title: You see sides of Kilimanjaro almost no one else does.
whyChoose.body: The route circles the rarely-visited northern slopes between Lemosho and the Kibo-Mawenzi saddle — terrain that other routes simply don't touch.

whyChoose.title: It's genuinely quiet.
whyChoose.body: The Northern Circuit remains one of the least-crowded ways up the mountain. Expect long stretches of trail with no other climbing parties in sight.

whyChoose.title: The acclimatisation profile is exceptional.
whyChoose.body: A long, gradual circumnavigation with steady altitude gain gives your body more time to adapt than any faster route — exactly what makes the extra days worth it on summit night.

northern-circuit.arrivalDay: You arrive in Tanzania and transfer to your hotel in Moshi. Your lead guide meets you for a thorough pre-climb briefing — gear check, route overview, altitude safety protocol, and Q&A. The Northern Circuit is the longest route we run, so take the time to ask every question you have. Rest well — your expedition begins tomorrow.

itinerary.title: Londorossi Gate → Mti Mkubwa Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Mti Mkubwa · Elevation: 2,780m · Distance: 6 km · Hiking Time: 2–3 hours
itinerary.body: A 4x4 drive up the forest track to the Lemosho Glades starts the day before the trail begins on foot. This is the most vegetation- and wildlife-rich section of the route — watch the canopy for monkeys as you climb through rainforest.
itinerary.expect: A gentle opening day. Use it to settle into the rhythm of the trail.

itinerary.title: Mti Mkubwa → Shira Ridge → Shira 1 Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Shira 1 Camp · Elevation: 3,600m · Distance: 8 km · Hiking Time: 4–5 hours
itinerary.body: The trees thin quickly today as the trail climbs the dramatic Shira Ridge. It's a steep day, rewarded with gorgeous panoramic views across the western Shira Plateau.
itinerary.expect: A sustained climb with real altitude gain. Mild headaches tonight are normal.

itinerary.title: Shira Plateau → Shira 2 Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Shira 2 Camp · Elevation: 3,850m · Distance: 8 km · Hiking Time: 4–5 hours
itinerary.body: A gentler day crossing the Shira Plateau's open meadows — good for acclimatisation. Short exploratory trails around camp let you get a feel for the surrounding moorland.
itinerary.expect: A comfortable day by comparison. Take advantage of the shorter distance to rest well.

itinerary.title: Shira 2 → Lava Tower → Moir Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Moir Camp · Elevation: 4,200m · Distance: 14 km · Hiking Time: 5–7 hours
itinerary.body: The trail passes through the Garden of Senecios — the last of the larger vegetation — before lunch at the dramatic Lava Tower rock formation. Here the Northern Circuit splits away from the southern circuit routes, entering alpine desert and the quieter northern half of the mountain.
itinerary.expect: A long day with a significant altitude touch at the Lava Tower. This is where the Northern Circuit begins to feel genuinely remote.

itinerary.title: Moir Valley → Buffalo Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Buffalo Camp · Elevation: 4,020m · Distance: 12 km · Hiking Time: 5–6 hours
itinerary.body: A moderately steep trail circles Kibo's northern slopes, with gradual inclines and declines and the option to hike Little Lent Hill for extended views. Buffalo Camp itself is a highlight of the Northern Circuit — a genuinely secluded camp few climbers on other routes ever see.
itinerary.expect: Rolling terrain rather than a single hard climb. The seclusion here is the whole point — enjoy it.

itinerary.title: Buffalo Ridge → Third Cave Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Third Cave Camp · Elevation: 3,875m · Distance: 8 km · Hiking Time: 5–7 hours
itinerary.body: The trail climbs Buffalo Ridge before skirting the remote northern slopes toward Third Cave Camp, near where the Rongai route passes. By now your body is well adjusted to high elevation.
itinerary.expect: A long day, but your acclimatisation advantage should be showing by this point in the trek.

itinerary.title: Kibo-Mawenzi Saddle → School Hut Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: School Hut Camp · Elevation: 4,800m · Distance: 15 km · Hiking Time: 4–5 hours
itinerary.body: A steeper climb today, crossing the saddle between Kibo and Mawenzi Peaks with unique views of both. An early dinner and early night follow — the wake-up call is midnight.
itinerary.expect: Nerves and altitude-related restlessness are normal tonight. Rest even if you can't sleep.

itinerary.title: Summit Night → Uhuru Peak → Millennium Camp
itinerary.meta: Camp: Millennium Camp · Elevation: 3,950m · Ascent: 5 km · Descent: 12 km · Total Time: 10–15 hours
itinerary.body: Midnight departure for the steep ascent to Gilman's Point, where you join climbers from other routes for the final push. The crater rim walk passes striking views of Mawenzi Peak before the last scramble through snow to Uhuru Peak. The long descent continues down to Millennium Camp.
itinerary.expect: The hardest and most extraordinary day of the expedition. The descent afterward is long — pace yourself.

itinerary.title: Millennium Camp → Mweka Gate → Hotel
itinerary.meta: End of Expedition · Elevation: 1,640m · Distance: 10 km · Hiking Time: 3–4 hours
itinerary.body: Breathing gets easier with every step down as the trail returns to rainforest. At Mweka Gate, your summit certificate is presented before the transfer back to your hotel in Moshi.
itinerary.expect: Rest. Celebrate. You've completed Kilimanjaro's longest route.

destinations.introBody: Tanzania protects more land under conservation than almost any other country on Earth — 28% of its total land area. This extraordinary commitment produces an unrivalled density of wildlife across three distinct safari circuits, each offering a completely different experience. The Northern Circuit delivers the iconic Serengeti and Ngorongoro classics; the Southern Circuit rewards those seeking true wilderness solitude; and the Western Circuit opens the door to chimpanzees, hippo spectacles, and Africa's largest lake. At EWA Safari Outfitters — born and based in Arusha — these are our home parks.
destinations.migrationDesc: The Migration never stops — it just moves. Calving in the Serengeti's south (Jan–Feb), north through the Seronera (Mar–Jun), Grumeti River crossings in the west (Jun–Jul), dramatic Mara River crossings in the north (Jul–Oct), then back south again. We design itineraries around wherever the herds are.

kenya.introBody: Kenya has inspired safari travellers for over a century — and for good reason. It is home to the planet's greatest wildlife spectacle (the Great Migration), the last two northern white rhinos on Earth, some of Africa's finest luxury lodges, and a coastline of extraordinary beauty. At EWA Safari Outfitters, we design Kenya safaris that go beyond the obvious — combining iconic reserves with hidden gems, conservation experiences, and deep cultural encounters for a journey that resonates long after you return home.
kenya.migrationCalloutBody: Over 1.5 million wildebeest and 500,000 zebra make an epic clockwise loop between Tanzania's Serengeti and Kenya's Masai Mara, driven by rainfall and fresh grazing. The Mara River crossings — where thousands of animals plunge through crocodile-infested water — occur July to October. Combine Kenya and Tanzania for the full Migration experience year-round.
kenya.comboBody: Kenya and Tanzania share the Great Rift Valley, the Serengeti–Mara ecosystem, and Kilimanjaro's shadow. Together they form the world's premier safari circuit. At EWA Safari Outfitters, we specialise in cross-border itineraries that seamlessly combine the best of both countries — Masai Mara crossings, Serengeti plains, Ngorongoro Crater, Amboseli elephants, and Zanzibar beaches — in one unforgettable journey.

kenya.birdingBody: With over 1,100 recorded bird species — including the rare Shoebill, Jackson's Widowbird, and the Abyssinian Ground Hornbill — Kenya is a birder's paradise. Lake Nakuru's flamingos, Samburu's Somali ostrich, and the Masai Mara's raptors are just the beginning.

rwanda.introBody: Rwanda has undergone one of the most extraordinary transformations in modern history — from tragedy to triumph, it is today one of Africa's safest, cleanest, and most forward-thinking nations. For wildlife lovers, Rwanda offers something no other country can match: the intimate experience of sitting with a family of mountain gorillas in ancient volcanic forest. Combined with chimpanzee trekking, Big Five safaris, pristine lakes, and the remarkable warmth of the Rwandan people, it is a destination that leaves every visitor changed.
rwanda.permitSectionBody: Rwanda issues just 96 gorilla permits per day (8 per habituated family, 12 families). Permits are in high demand year-round and sell out months ahead for peak season. We handle all permit bookings as part of your itinerary — contact us early for the best availability.
rwanda.comboBody: Rwanda's gorillas and Tanzania's Serengeti plains are the two most iconic wildlife experiences in Africa. itineraries.park1Desc: Home of the Great Migration — 1.5 million wildebeest moving across endless plains.
itineraries.park2Desc: The world's largest intact volcanic caldera sheltering all of the Big Five.

itineraries.faq4q: What animals will I see on safari?
itineraries.faq4a: East Africa is home to the Big Five — lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo and rhino — plus cheetah, giraffe, zebra, hippo, crocodile, wild dog, and over 500 bird species. The exact species depend on which parks you visit and the time of year.
itineraries.faq5q: When is the best time to visit Tanzania?
itineraries.faq5a: June to October is the dry season: vegetation is sparse, animals gather at water sources, and the Serengeti Migration peaks. January to March brings the calving season — spectacular for predator action. December and April–May are the rainy months and offer lower prices.
itineraries.faq6q: When is the best time to visit Kenya?
itineraries.faq6a: July to October is prime time — the Great Migration's famous river crossings happen in the Masai Mara between August and October. Kenya's dry seasons (January–February and June–October) offer the best game viewing year-round.
itineraries.faq7q: What is the difference between a Tanzania and a Kenya safari?
itineraries.faq7a: Tanzania offers more parks, more wilderness, and the largest protected land area in Africa — Serengeti, Ngorongoro and the southern circuit are extraordinary. Kenya's Masai Mara is unmatched for big-cat density and Migration river crossings. Many travellers combine both for the ultimate East Africa experience.
itineraries.faq8q: What is the Great Wildebeest Migration?
itineraries.faq8a: The annual movement of over 1.5 million wildebeest, 250,000 zebra and 500,000 gazelle in a clockwise loop through the Serengeti and Masai Mara ecosystem. Calving happens in Ndutu (Jan–Mar), the herds move north through June, and the dramatic Mara River crossings occur from July to October.
itineraries.faq9q: Is safari travel safe for families with children?
itineraries.faq9a: Absolutely. We run family safaris regularly and tailor every itinerary to children's ages and interests. Most game lodges welcome children over 5, and private vehicles mean you can move at your family's pace. Our guides are trained in child-friendly game drives.
itineraries.faq10q: What vaccinations and health precautions are required?
itineraries.faq10a: Yellow fever vaccination is required if arriving from a yellow fever country. We strongly recommend anti-malarial medication, hepatitis A, typhoid and tetanus boosters. Consult your travel health clinic 6–8 weeks before departure. We provide a comprehensive health briefing with every booking.

travelInfo.heroSubtitle: Everything you need to know before your Tanzania safari or Kilimanjaro trek — from the best time to visit and health requirements to packing essentials and currency.
travelInfo.qf5Value: Required for most nationalities — available on arrival or e-visa online ($50 USD)
travelInfo.qf6Value: Expected: $10–20/day for guides; $5–10/day for camp staff
travelInfo.s1b1: Tanzania is extraordinary in every month of the year — there is always somewhere remarkable to go and something unmissable to see. That said, the season you visit shapes your experience significantly, so choosing the right time for your priorities matters.
travelInfo.s1b2: The dry season from June to October is widely considered the best time for wildlife viewing. The vegetation thins, animals concentrate around permanent water sources, and roads are at their most accessible. The Great Migration river crossings in the northern Serengeti peak in July and August. Expect clear skies, comfortable daytime temperatures, and cooler evenings. Book well in advance — this is the most in-demand period.
travelInfo.s1h3: November to May — Wet Season (Green Season)
travelInfo.s1b3: The short rains (November) and long rains (March–May) bring lush, dramatically green landscapes and significantly fewer tourists. December to March is particularly rewarding: the calving season in the Ndutu area of the southern Serengeti delivers extraordinary predator-prey drama as 8,000 wildebeest calves are born every day. Accommodation prices are lower, parks are quieter, and birdlife is at its most spectacular. Some camps close in April and May, and roads in the southern parks can become impassable.
travelInfo.s1tr1c3: Calving season, Ndutu; fewer tourists; excellent predator action
travelInfo.s1tr2c3: Lush landscape; green season discounts; some camps closed
travelInfo.s1tr3c3: Peak wildlife; Mara River crossings (Jul–Oct); best visibility
travelInfo.s1tr4c3: Good value; excellent birding; landscape greening
travelInfo.s1tr5c3: Quiet parks; herds moving south; pleasant weather
travelInfo.s2b1: Under International Health Regulations, travellers arriving from yellow fever endemic countries must present a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate. We advise all clients to consult a travel health clinic or GP at least six to eight weeks before departure. Recommended vaccinations for Tanzania typically include hepatitis A, typhoid, and tetanus. Proof of COVID-19 status requirements should be checked against current government guidance close to your departure date.
travelInfo.s2b2: Tanzania is a malaria zone. Consult your doctor about an appropriate antimalarial medication before you travel — options include Malarone, Doxycycline, and Lariam, each with different profiles and suitability. In addition to medication, bring a DEET-based insect repellent and pack long-sleeved clothing for evenings. Mosquito nets are provided at all lodges and camps we use.
travelInfo.s2b3: Comprehensive travel health insurance is mandatory before travelling to Tanzania. We strongly recommend taking out a temporary AMREF Flying Doctor Service membership, which covers emergency medical evacuation from remote areas across East Africa — an important safeguard when you are in the wilderness, hours from the nearest hospital.
travelInfo.s3b1: Tanzania's official currency is the Tanzanian Shilling (TZS). US Dollars are widely accepted for safari expenses, tips, and major purchases. We recommend bringing a mix of USD cash (in clean, undamaged bills printed after 2009) and a Visa or Mastercard for city use. ATMs are available in Arusha, Dar es Salaam, and Zanzibar.
travelInfo.s3b2: Currency exchange is available at Kilimanjaro and Julius Nyerere international airports, all major commercial banks, and licensed bureau de change offices in Arusha and other towns. Avoid exchanging money with unofficial street dealers.
travelInfo.s3b3: Personal items such as cameras, binoculars, and laptops are imported duty-free. Professional or commercial filming equipment, musical instruments, and recording devices may require a customs bond guaranteeing re-export — check with the Tanzania Revenue Authority before travelling if you are bringing extensive gear. Firearms and hunting weapons require a special import permit obtained in advance. Retain receipts for all souvenir and handicraft purchases, and ensure any wildlife trophies are accompanied by proper CITES documentation for presentation at customs on departure.
travelInfo.s4b1: Safari vehicles, light aircraft, and bush camps all impose practical luggage limits. Soft-sided bags are strongly preferred over rigid suitcases — they compress into luggage compartments more easily. For fly-in safaris, most light aircraft operators enforce a 15 kg soft-bag limit per person. Pack efficiently and leave the wheeled suitcase at your Arusha or Nairobi hotel for days spent in the bush.
travelInfo.s4b2: Neutral, muted colours — khaki, olive, beige, tan, brown — are the safari standard. Bright colours and white attract insects and can startle wildlife; patterns are harder for animals to read than solid neutrals. Natural fibres such as cotton and linen breathe well in the heat. A light fleece or down jacket is essential for cold mornings and evenings, particularly in the Ngorongoro highlands and at altitude on Kilimanjaro. Long sleeves and trousers at dusk reduce mosquito exposure.
travelInfo.s4list1: Light, neutral-coloured shirts and trousers (cotton or linen)
travelInfo.s4list2: Fleece or lightweight down jacket for mornings and evenings
travelInfo.s4list3: Comfortable, broken-in walking shoes or light trail runners
travelInfo.s4list7: Swimsuit — for lodges, beach extensions, and boat safaris
travelInfo.s4list10: Power bank — electricity in remote camps can be intermittent
travelInfo.s5b1: Tanzania is one of the most stable and safe countries in sub-Saharan Africa, with a long record of peaceful tourism. The national parks are accessed in dedicated safari vehicles with certified guides — the risk profile inside the parks is extremely low. As in any country, exercise normal awareness in urban areas, avoid displaying expensive equipment in crowded places, and keep copies of your passport and travel documents.
travelInfo.s5b2: Follow your guide's instructions at all times when in or near wildlife areas. Do not exit the vehicle except at designated areas or with a certified armed ranger escort. Never approach wildlife on foot without a guide. At night in camps and lodges, do not walk between tents alone if wildlife may be present — camp staff will escort you.
